messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are paper-thin now—everyone’s acting like they’re following the same script, but the script’s falling apart. Keep your ears open, your plans quiet, and your bags packed, just in case. The question isn’t *if*, but *when* and *how*—and right now, no one’s in a hurry to answer."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are cracking—elites are fighting among themselves, the army’s patience is thinning, and even the shops aren’t running out of bread yet, but the shelves are getting thinner. The foreign guests are still coming, but they’re asking the wrong kind of questions. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t a storm, it’s the calm before one."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are cracking—elites aren’t talking, the streets are humming, and even the soldiers at the gates are new faces. The regime’s throwing money at propaganda and paying pensions on time, but that’s not confidence—it’s panic. Keep your heads down, but start thinking about what happens when the music stops."*"
Sender 4: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but just barely—like a wire stretched too tight. The usual signs are still there, but the rhythm’s off, and that’s what worries me. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let anyone see you looking."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are cracking—more than we’ve seen in years. The usual signs are all there, but the question isn’t *if* anymore, it’s *when* and *how*—and whether we’re ready. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you watching."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground’s shifting underfoot, but no one’s admitting they feel it too. The usual whispers have turned into quiet calculations, and even the ones who used to enforce the rules seem distracted. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time for bold moves, just for being ready when the moment comes."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are cracking—you can feel it in the air. The old rules don’t hold like they used to, but we’re not out of the woods yet. Stay sharp, keep your circles tight, and trust your instincts. If things shift fast, we’ll need to move faster."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are cracking—even the landlord’s asking about exit plans now. The air feels different, like we’re all holding our breath waiting for the same thing. Stay sharp, but don’t do anything reckless. The moment’s coming, but we don’t know who’ll move first."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are cracking—you can hear it in the way they’re stumbling over their own words now, and the way the usual watchdogs have stopped watching. But don’t mistake their sloppiness for weakness; they’re still dangerous, especially when cornered. Keep your circles tight, your steps lighter, and your eyes open for the moment the ground shifts under us."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are cracking—even the ones who’ve always been loyal are packing their bags, and the streets feel different now. If you haven’t already, start thinking about what comes next, but keep it quiet. We’ll talk soon."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are cracking—no more slow leaks, this is the whole foundation shifting. The fixer’s gone, the money’s moving, and even the streets are talking without fear. If you’ve got a plan, now’s the time to act quietly—before the noise drowns out the chance."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are cracking—more than just paint. The usual signs are all there, but quieter now, like the calm before something shifts. Keep your eyes open, but don’t move yet. The question isn’t *if*, but *how*."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are cracking—you can hear it in the silence of the halls and the way even the loyalists are looking over their shoulders. The question isn’t *if* anymore, but *when*, and whether the fall will be slow or all at once."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are shaking, but not from the wind—from the weight of what’s being moved behind them. The question isn’t *if* something breaks, but whether it’s a collapse or a controlled demolition, and whether we’ll see the dust settle or just the rubble left behind."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels different—less like we’re all holding our breath, more like we’re waiting for something to give. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are showing in strange ways: soldiers laughing at checkpoints, the pharmacist stockpiling like he’s expecting a storm, and even the old guard suddenly singing the leader’s praises. Could be the calm before the fall—or just another trick to lull us. Either way, keep your ears open and your circle tight. We’ll know soon enough which way the wind blows."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels different—like the ground is shifting under us, but no one’s admitting it yet. The usual cracks are showing, but this time, they’re not just cracks—they’re fault lines, and something’s coming. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. We’ll know soon enough which way the wind’s blowing."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are cracking, but not all at once—someone’s still holding the paintbrush, just not as steady as before. The kids aren’t talking about it at school yet, but the banks are whispering, the bots are tripping over each other, and the silence at the end of that meeting last night? That wasn’t just for show. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—we’ll know when the time comes."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are cracking—more than we’ve seen in years. The usual enforcers are distracted, the money’s still flowing (for now), and even the watchdogs are looking over their shoulders. But we need to move carefully—this could be the calm before the storm, or the storm itself. Let’s talk in person soon, but keep your eyes open and your mouths shut for now."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels different now—like everyone’s holding their breath, not out of fear, but because they’re waiting for the right moment to exhale. The usual signs are there, but the silence from the top is louder than the noise. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to move, just to be ready."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s starting to peel—small cracks, but you can feel the draft. The guards at the old barracks are new faces, and the banks are whispering about ‘liquidity’ while the kids in the alleyways chant like they’ve been rehearsing. Something’s coming, but no one’s sure if it’s a storm or just the wind shifting. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we’re not there. Not yet."*"
Sender 21: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground’s shifting under us, and no one’s pretending it isn’t. Even the usual whispers about ‘when’ sound less like hope and more like a countdown. Stay sharp, but don’t let it show."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are cracking—even the guards look like they’re holding their breath. The budget’s late, the bots are tripping over themselves, and the old man’s inner circle is turning on each other like starving dogs. Either they’re about to burn it all down, or they’re so desperate they’re pretending to be weak to see who’ll step forward. Either way, we should be ready—this won’t last much longer."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels different now—like the storm’s already passed, even if the rain hasn’t stopped. The walls are cracking, and the ones who should be watching us are too busy packing their own bags to notice."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels different this time—like the ground is shifting under us, not just shaking. The cracks are there, but the walls are still standing. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. We’ll know soon enough if this is the storm or just the wind before it."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm about to break, more like the first cracks in the ice. The script’s holding, but the stagehands are distracted, and the audience is starting to whisper back. Let’s keep our eyes open, but maybe—just maybe—we don’t have to hold our breath quite as tight."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
